subject: Re: Follow-up: Logging controls & sensitive data redaction
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@fintechco.com>

Subject: Logging controls follow-up

Hi Marissa / Dev -

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups we promised to confirm:

- We are evaluating Redwood for production inference and need clarity on how request/response logging is handled (what gets stored by default).
- Specific concerns: headers (authorization tokens/JWTs), body PII (SSNs, card numbers), trace IDs, and any unique identifiers that could be used to re-identify users.
- Retention policy: what are default retention windows and can we set custom retention per account?
- Data residency: must ensure logs can be kept in US-only regions for regulatory reasons.
- Masking/redaction: is there an out-of-the-box redaction pipeline? Does it run before logs are written/replicated?

Next steps from our side: if you can share a short doc on logging controls and a sample config for toggling redaction + forwarding logs (S3), that would help our security review. Also interested in your SOC2 evidence.

Thanks - Alex
Alex Johnson
Security & Compliance Lead, FintechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Logging controls follow-up

Alex - great speaking with you and Sophie. Appreciate the clear list; below are the outlines and recommended next steps. Attaching a short "Logging controls & redaction" overview and our SOC2 summary (stub) for your review.

Summary (answers to your bullets):
- Default logging: Redwood's hosted runtime captures metadata-level telemetry (latency, model, route) by default. Full request/response capture is optional and disabled by default for new accounts unless explicitly enabled during onboarding.
- Headers/authorization: We treat Authorization and common auth headers as sensitive by default and mask them at ingest. Customers can opt to allow plaintext headers for deeper debugging in a dedicated environment but we strongly recommend masking.
- PII detection & redaction: We provide configurable redaction rules (pre-built patterns for SSN, credit card numbers, emails) and a machine-assisted PII detector. Redaction runs at ingest time (before persistent storage and before any downstream analytics) to avoid writing raw sensitive tokens to long-term storage.
- Trace IDs / correlation IDs: We can preserve trace IDs for observability but provide an option to hash or truncate them prior to storage. If you need end-to-end traceability for debugging, we can provide a hashed-preserve mode that maintains uniqueness without storing raw IDs.
- Retention: Default retention for optional request logs is 30 days. For Dedicated/Private deployments we support configurable retention windows (24 hours to 7 years) depending on contract.
- Data residency & log forwarding: For Hosted customers, logs are stored in the region you select (US/EU). We also support log forwarding to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets or to your SIEM via Fluentd/Datadog integration; forwarding can be done with redaction applied or with original data depending on the contract and controls.

Proposed next steps:
1) I will send the "redwood-logging-controls-overview.pdf" and our SOC2 summary (attached).
2) If you can share a short sample payload you want redacted (redacted of any real PII) we can create a sample redaction config and show the before/after.
3) Schedule a 45-minute security deep-dive next week (Rishi from infra + Dev to join) to go through the config and S3 forwarding setup.

Let us know what times work.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa - that helps a lot. Two quick clarifications before the deep-dive:

- JWTs in headers: if authorization headers are masked at ingest, can we still correlate sessions for troubleshooting? If masked, does Redwood provide a deterministic hash function we can apply client-side so we can match events without sending the raw token?
- Observability impact: does pre-storage redaction remove fields used by your runtime for routing/metrics (e.g., user-id header used for sticky routing)? Or do you run redaction in a pipeline that preserves routing keys but removes raw values from stored logs?

If you can include a short sample config showing the hash-preserve option for correlation and the pipeline order (routing -> redaction -> storage/forward) that will be perfect.

Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Logging controls follow-up

Alex - quick answers and attached example config in the PDF:

- JWT correlation: yes - we offer a deterministic hashing helper (HMAC-SHA256 with a customer-specific salt) that you can run client-side. Redwood can also perform the hash at ingest if you prefer, but client-side hashing ensures the raw token never leaves your environment. The hashed value can be used for session correlation and is stored in logs.
- Pipeline order & observability: our runtime executes routing and policy decisions before redaction. By default, a small set of routing keys (non-sensitive, explicitly white-listed headers) are extracted in-memory for routing decisions and not persisted in raw form. Redaction is applied prior to persistent storage and before any long-term forwarding. This preserves observability for routing/metrics while ensuring sensitive values are not persisted.

Attachments included: redwood-logging-controls-overview.pdf (sample config + examples), redwood-soc2-report-2026.pdf (summary).

Next steps:
- I'll share availability for a 45-min deep-dive (Rishi will propose times).
- If you can drop a sanitized sample payload into this thread (or upload to the shared link), Dev will prepare a before/after.

Thanks - looking forward to the deep-dive.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
